successors.name: Dutch East Indies
successors.text: Palembang annexed by the Dutch in June 1821; 'Dutch rule would last from June 1821 to December 27, 1949'

ledger.x: 1459: Palembang appears in the record as a Javanese-dependent principality (Cliopatria's first shape); the page dates no founding.
1659: Palembang is proclaimed a sultanate by Susuhunan Abdurrahman.
Late 17th century: Bangka falls to Palembang by inheritance; tin is found c.

1812: Bangka is ceded to Britain after Sultan Mahmud Badaruddin II is removed (his reign ends 14 May 1812; he had massacred the Dutch post's staff on Bangka during the British invasion of Java in 1811).

wars.name: Dutch punitive expedition to Palembang
wars.outcome: The Dutch burnt the city in 1659 and razed Kuto Gawang after a Dutch ship was attacked in 1657; the court moved to Beringin Janggut and the sultanate was proclaimed that year.

wars.name: British invasion of Java and the 1811 Bangka incident
wars.outcome: Sultan Mahmud Badaruddin II attacked and massacred the Dutch post's staff on Bangka in 1811; he was removed by the British and his successor ceded Bangka to Britain in 1812.

wars.name: First Dutch expedition to Palembang
wars.outcome: Dutch forces under Wolterbeek were defeated in 1819; fortified river coasts blocked a naval assault.

wars.name: Second Dutch expedition to Palembang
wars.outcome: The Dutch under Hendrik Merkus de Kock defeated the sultanate's forces and annexed Palembang in June 1821; the sultanate was dissolved on 7 October 1823.

certainty.note: Riverine and coastal reach of a Musi-based state; no treaty line is dated by the pages opened.
The cession of Bangka (1812, confirmed by the Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1814) is a dated transfer of an island; the mainland frontiers stay approximate.
